Deviation from linearity was always seen in the period preceding the exponential phase (lag period). Here, perfect straight lines were obtained, if the In(OD 600) values were plotted against the squared times (Fig. 3A, inset). As outlined in in the supplemental material, this implies that the specific growth during the lag phase increases linearly in time (Fig. 1B and 2B). Also, the specific methane-forming activity increased linearly in time during this period (Fig. 1B and 2B). In fact, a plot of the 9CH, values against the corresponding u values showed a direct proportional relationship between both parameters, the slope representing the reciprocal of the specific growth yield (YcH.), which now was constant (Fig. 1C, 2C, and 3A). The physiological meaning of these findings is that, after inoculation, cells adapt to the new growth condition by the uniform and concerted acceleration of their specific growth rate and specific methane-forming activity in a way that YCH, remains fixed. The specific growth rates became maximal at the entry of the exponential stage and remained constant throughout the particular stage (Fig. 1B, 2B, and 3A). The values did not significantly differ among the various gassing regimens (0.22 to 0.25 h-1; doubling times of 2.8 to 3.1 h) (Table 3). However, the 9CH, was not constant. Specific methane-forming activities initially increased to a maximum and declined thereafter. The decline occurred concomitant with the decrease in the dissolved hydrogen partial pressures, resulting from the increasing hydrogen uptake rates by the growing biomass (Fig. 1 and 2 and Table 3). Apparently, the physiology of the cells continuously changed, even at a constant growth rate. After exponential growth, the cells entered the linear phase. During this stage, the specific growth rates and specific methane-forming activities, calculated by using the equations S.5 and S.6, respectively, in the supplemental material(1), decreased in parallel (Fig. 1B and 2B). Moreover, 9CH,-versus-u plots showed the direct proportional relationship as expected from equation S.8 (Fig. 1C, 2C, and 3B).
